To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) PPARa and PPARb/d are activated by fatty acids (arachidic acid and cyclopentenonic prostaglandins) and by NSAID, and 2) PPARa, b/d, and g regulate the expression of genes involved in the inflammatory response by direct binding to the promoter of these genes, and by indirect effects, e.g. by the modulation of the expression of antioxidant genes and the inactivation of the NF kB signalling pathway.
PPARa and PPARg are involved in the modulation of NF kB activity, which is the key transcription factor of the pro inflammatory reaction.
PPARs are transcription factors that are involved in the regulation of the inflammatory reaction and that they are activated by oxidised, nitrated and cyclopentenonic fatty acids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the mechanisms of action of PPAR in inflammatory reactions, especially in the context of their role in the modulation of NF kB activity.
the identification of PPAR activators and their mechanisms of action in order to develop novel anti inflammatory drugs.
the study of the anti-inflammatory effects of fatty acid derivatives and cyclopentenones, which act as ligands for the PPAR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PPARs play an important role in the control of the inflammatory reaction by regulating the expression of a wide range of inflammatory genes, including those that encode proinflammatory cytokines, chemokines, adhesion molecules and inducible enzymes.
the PPAR family of transcription factors plays an important role in the self regulation of the inflammatory reaction.
PPARs play a role as a negative regulator of the inflammatory reaction by inhibiting the NF kB pathway.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PPARa/b/d play an important role in the inflammatory response, especially in the modulation of pro inflammatory mediators, and thus in the regulation of the inflammatory reaction.
PPAR are important transcription factors that regulate the inflammatory response.
PPARa and PPARb/d are involved in the regulation of the acute inflammatory response, whereas PPARg is involved in the chronic inflammatory response.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PPAR are involved in the modulation of inflammatory reactions.
PPAR are important modulators of the inflammatory response.
PPAR are involved in the regulation of inflammatory reactions and that their activation is a promising therapeutic strategy.
